title: Clocks & Calendars
relevance: Campus SDE OAs and aptitude screens routinely test clock-hand relative motion and calendar odd-day modular arithmetic for fast, exact quantitative reasoning.

phases.goal: Establish clock-hand speeds, the angle formula, and odd-day / leap-year calendar basics.

must_hit.point: Minute hand moves 6°/min; hour hand moves 0.5°/min; relative closing speed is 5.5°/min.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both hand speeds and their difference 5.5°/min as the closing rate.

must_hit.point: Angle between hands at H hours and M minutes is θ = |30H − 5.5M|°.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes or applies the absolute-value formula with 30H and 5.5M.

must_hit.point: Odd days are total days mod 7, mapped 0=Sun, 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 3=Wed, 4=Thu, 5=Fri, 6=Sat.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines odd days as remainder on ÷7 and gives the Sunday=0 through Saturday=6 map.

must_hit.point: Normal year: 365 days ≡ 1 odd day; leap year: 366 days ≡ 2 odd days.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States 1 weekday advance for a normal year and 2 for a leap year via odd days.

must_hit.point: A year is leap if divisible by 4, except century years which must be divisible by 400; century odd days are 100→5, 200→3, 300→1, 400→0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the ÷4 / century-÷400 leap rule and the 5, 3, 1, 0 century odd-day cycle.

probes: What are the minute-hand, hour-hand, and relative speeds, and what is the angle formula at H:M?
What is an odd day, and how do normal vs leap years change the weekday?

hints.1: Relate each hand’s degrees per minute, and think of weekdays as days mod 7.
hints.2: Full circle in 60 minutes for the minute hand; hour hand advances 0.5° per minute; odd-day labels start at Sunday = 0.
hints.3: Minute 6°/min, hour 0.5°/min, relative 5.5°/min; θ = |30H − 5.5M|°; 365 ≡ 1 and 366 ≡ 2 odd days; leap if ÷4 except century ÷400.

phases.goal: Apply coincidence/opposite/right-angle solving, daily counts, faulty-clock ratios, and odd-day weekday calculation.

must_hit.point: Hands coincide every 65 5/11 minutes (720/11); solve coincidence by setting |30H − 5.5M| = 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses 65 5/11 or 720/11 and sets the angle formula to 0° for the minute mark.

must_hit.point: In a 24-hour day: coincide 22 times, opposite 22 times, right angles 44 times.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the triple 22, 22, 44 and notes the missing cases around 12:00 / 6:00 in each 12 hours.

must_hit.point: For a gaining/losing clock, form True:Shown from how many hours the faulty clock shows in 24 true hours, then scale elapsed shown time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Builds a ratio like 24 over shown hours in a day and multiplies by elapsed shown time.

must_hit.point: Day of week = cumulative odd days from centuries, intervening years (leap×2 + normal×1), and month/day totals, all mod 7.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks century blocks + year leap/normal odd days + month remainders, then maps the residue to a weekday.

probes: How many times per day do the hands coincide, point opposite, and form right angles?
How do you find the true time when a clock loses or gains a fixed amount every 24 hours?

hints.1: For perfect clocks, start from the angle equation; for faulty clocks, compare shown time to true time over a day.
hints.2: Coincide/opposite miss once per 12 hours near 12:00/6:00; right angles occur 22 times per 12 hours. Ratio True/Shown uses 24 true hours vs 24±gain/loss.
hints.3: Daily counts are 22, 22, 44; perfect overlap interval is 65 5/11 min; e.g. lose 16 min/24 h → shown 356/15 h and True/Shown = 90/89.

phases.goal: Choose the correct calendar-repetition case and inner vs reflex angle interpretation.

must_hit.point: Calendar repeats when net odd days are a multiple of 7 and year type matches; by leap offset: Leap+1 → 6 years, Leap+2 → 11, Leap+3 → 11, leap year itself → 28.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the odd-day multiple-of-7 condition and the 6 / 11 / 11 / 28 shortcut by leap-year position.

must_hit.point: Reflex angle between hands is 360° minus the inner angle from θ = |30H − 5.5M|°.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Computes the formula angle first, then subtracts from 360° when reflex is asked.

must_hit.point: If hands overlap every 64 minutes of true time instead of 65 5/11, the clock is gaining (e.g. 32 8/11 min per 1440-minute day).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares 64 to 65 5/11, concludes gain, and can quote total gain 32 8/11 min/day.

probes: When does a year’s calendar repeat, and how does leap-year position change the gap?
If asked for the reflex angle between clock hands, what do you compute after the formula angle?

hints.1: Repetition needs both weekday alignment and matching leap/normal type; reflex is the long way around the dial.
hints.2: Locate the year as Leap+1/+2/+3 or leap itself; for reflex, subtract the smaller angle from a full circle.

phases.goal: Map odd-day and clock rules onto OA-style scheduling cycles and mirror-image time.

must_hit.point: A 15-day cadence is 2 weeks and 1 day, so each occurrence shifts +1 weekday; a weekend landing shifts to the following Monday.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Tracks Tuesday→…→Saturday for the 5th slot, then applies the Monday shift rule.

must_hit.point: For a k-day reboot cycle to start on the same weekday again, elapsed days must be a multiple of 7; minimum is LCM(k, 7) (e.g. LCM(5, 7) = 35).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States needing a common multiple of cycle length and 7, and gives 35 for a 5-day cycle.

must_hit.point: Vertical mirror clock: actual time = 11:60 − shown time (mirror + true = 12 hours; between 12:00 and 1:00 use 23:60).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Applies 11:60 − shown (e.g. 3:40 → 8:20) and mentions the 12-hour sum check.

probes: A job runs every 15 days but weekends slide to Monday—how do you find the weekday of the 5th run?
A 5-day online/offline cycle starts Sunday; when can it start on Sunday again?
A vertical mirror shows 3:40—what is the real time?

hints.1: Reduce the period mod 7 for weekday shift; for mirrors, true and shown times sum to 12 hours.
hints.2: 15 days ≡ 1 weekday; weekend → next Monday. Same weekday restart needs LCM with 7. Mirror: subtract from 11:60.
hints.3: 5th of a Tue start lands Saturday then Monday; LCM(5,7)=35; 11:60 − 3:40 = 8:20.

tradeoffs.topic: Normal year vs leap year (weekday advance)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Normal year 365 days ≡ 1 odd day (advances 1 weekday); leap year 366 days ≡ 2 odd days (advances 2 weekdays).
Leap+1 repeats in 6 years; Leap+2 or Leap+3 in 11 years; a leap year itself in 28 years—only when net odd days are a multiple of 7 and leap/normal type matches.
Compute θ = |30H − 5.5M|° first; if reflex is required, answer 360° − θ (e.g. 10:25 → 162.5° inner, 197.5° reflex).

tradeoffs.topic: Overlap interval shorter vs longer than 65 5/11 min
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Perfect overlap every 720/11 = 65 5/11 min; overlapping in only 64 true minutes means the clock is gaining (gain 32 8/11 min per 1440-minute day in the worked case).

gotchas.trap: Thinking the minute hand closes on the hour hand at 6°/min.
gotchas.correction: The hour hand also moves at 0.5°/min, so relative closing speed is 5.5°/min; almost all clock times use this 5.5 divisor.

gotchas.trap: Treating every 4th year as a leap year with no exception.
gotchas.correction: A century year is leap only if divisible by 400; 1900 and 2100 are not leap years, but 2000 is.

gotchas.trap: Assuming coincide / opposite / right-angle counts of 24, 24, 48 in a day.
gotchas.correction: Correct daily counts are 22 coincide, 22 opposite, and 44 right angles (11+11 and 22+22 per two 12-hour halves, with misses near 12:00 and 6:00).

gotchas.trap: Believing any weekday can be the last day of a century.
gotchas.correction: Century odd-day residues only yield Friday, Wednesday, Monday, or Sunday as last days; Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday are impossible.
